related_questions.question: What are the four stages of viral pneumonia?

text_blocks.snippet: Viral pneumonia progresses through four stages: congestion, red hepatization, grey hepatization, and resolution. These stages describe the physical changes in the lungs and the progression of symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: congestion, red hepatization, grey hepatization, and resolution

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of each stage:

list.title: 1. Congestion:
list.snippet: This initial stage occurs within the first 24 hours of infection and involves increased blood flow and swelling in the airways. Symptoms include a wet cough (possibly with clear, yellow, or green sputum), fever, fatigue, chest pain, and shortness of breath.

list.title: 2. Red Hepatization:
list.snippet: A few days after the onset of infection, this stage is characterized by the lungs becoming engorged with blood, resembling the consistency of the liver (hepatization). Symptoms may include a worsening cough with thicker, more copious sputum, and increased shortness of breath.

list.title: 3. Grey Hepatization:
list.snippet: This stage follows red hepatization and is marked by a lack of blood vessels in the affected lung tissue, giving it a grayish appearance. Symptoms can include continued shortness of breath and swelling and fibrous strands around the air sacs (alveoli).

list.title: 4. Resolution:
list.snippet: This final stage involves the immune system clearing the infection, with macrophages (immune cells) removing cellular debris and restoring the normal lung structure. Symptoms gradually subside, and the patient begins to feel better.
